name: Kristopher T. Kimmell
identity: Kristopher T. Kimmell, MD, FAANS — staff neurosurgeon at Rochester Regional Health (Rochester General Hospital) and clinical assistant professor of neurosurgery at the University of Rochester Medical Center, Rochester, NY.
bio: Kimmell is a board-certified general adult neurosurgeon at Rochester Regional Health who practices the full breadth of cranial and spine neurosurgery, including neuro-oncology, cerebrovascular disease, complex spine, trauma, and pain/movement disorders. He is the ROC account's active LITT operator, with internal claims data documenting NeuroBlate ablation cases for intracranial lesions/metastases. His scholarly interests center on comparative-effectiveness research, health economics, quality improvement, and patient safety in neurosurgery.
training: University of Oklahoma College of Medicine (MD, 2010) · Neurosurgery residency, Strong Memorial Hospital / University of Rochester · Fellowship not verified · Pedigree: URMC-trained, now dual-affiliated Rochester Regional Health + URMC clinical faculty
litt_exposure: Direct LITT operator on our platform — internal claims show 6 LITT procedures on NeuroBlate plus 11 brain-metastasis resections; cohort tagged 'LITT — Our Equipment (NeuroBlate).' He is the established Monteris user at this account.
wheelhouse: General adult neurosurgery — neuro-oncology (metastases, cranial tumors), cerebrovascular, complex/minimally invasive spine, trauma, pituitary and peripheral nerve; secondary academic focus on health economics and quality/safety research.
kol_note: Publication- and society-active (AANS involvement; systematic-review and quality/health-economics work), but not a national LITT thought leader. Best positioned as a loyal local champion and reference user for NeuroBlate rather than a podium KOL.

name: Vincent N. Nguyen
identity: Vincent N. Nguyen, MD — cerebrovascular/endovascular neurosurgeon and Assistant Professor, Department of Neurosurgery, University of Rochester Medical Center (Strong Memorial Hospital), Rochester, NY.
bio: Nguyen is an early-career vascular neurosurgeon at URMC offering both open microsurgical and endovascular treatment of cerebrovascular disease, with particular focus on EC-IC bypass for ischemic disease/Moyamoya, complex aneurysms, and spinal ischemia. He joined URMC after endovascular fellowship in 2023 and is research-active, with a body of systematic-review and technique work on adult Moyamoya and bypass. In the claims data he appears as a LITT-naive craniotomy surgeon and low-volume metastasis referrer, consistent with a vascular rather than tumor/ablation practice.
training: Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, University of Tennessee Health Science Center — Memphis (2015–2022) · Endovascular neurosurgery fellowship, Keck Hospital of USC (2022–2023) · Pedigree: UTHSC/Semmes-Murphey cerebrovascular training + USC endovascular
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience. Subspecialty is cerebrovascular/endovascular; claims show only 1 tumor craniotomy and 7 metastasis referrals with no LITT procedures (cohort 'LITT-Naive Craniotomy Surgeon').
wheelhouse: Cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery — Moyamoya, EC-IC/direct-indirect bypass, complex aneurysms, ischemic disease, spinal vascular pathology.
kol_note: Productive early-career academic with several peer-reviewed cerebrovascular papers, but no standing or publications in LITT/neuro-oncology ablation.

name: Kevin A. Walter
identity: Kevin A. Walter, MD — Professor of Neurosurgery and Oncology, Chief of Neurosurgery at UR Medicine's Highland Hospital, University of Rochester Medical Center; brain and spinal tumor surgeon, Rochester, NY.
bio: Walter is a senior academic neuro-oncologic neurosurgeon at URMC and one of the region's highest-volume brain-tumor surgeons, operating at both Strong Memorial and Rochester General Hospitals with expertise in image-guided surgery, radiosurgery, and complex spinal tumor surgery. He directs a translational neuro-oncology laboratory (co-led with Eleanor Carson-Walter, PhD) and has published extensively on intracranial metastasis and high-grade glioma. Despite this deep tumor-metastasis practice, claims data flag him as LITT-naive — a high-value conversion opportunity for image-guided ablation.
training: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, Johns Hopkins Hospital · NCI-sponsored neuro-oncology fellowship, Johns Hopkins · Faculty at University of Pittsburgh (director of adult neuro-oncology) before recruitment to University of Rochester in 2007 · Pedigree: Johns Hopkins neuro-oncology, top-tier
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience — cohort tagged 'LITT-Naive Craniotomy Surgeon.' However he is a high-volume metastasis/tumor surgeon (29 metastasis cases, tumor craniotomy) with established image-guided/stereotactic radiosurgery expertise, making him a strong latent LITT adopter.
wheelhouse: Neuro-oncology — high-grade glioma, brain and spinal metastasis, image-guided/stereotactic tumor surgery, radiosurgery, complex spinal tumors; translational brain-tumor laboratory research.
kol_note: Academic leader: full Professor, division/hospital chief, former director of adult neuro-oncology at Pittsburgh, NCI-trained, laboratory director, and prolific author on glioma and metastasis. Carries real regional and academic weight in neuro-oncology — a marquee target whose adoption would validate NeuroBlate at the account.
